headline: Slow bleed: bond-market jitters, frontier defaults and tariff creep sap a tired world

events: US extends Section 232 tariffs to more electronics and pharma inputs; China answers with tighter rare-earth and graphite licensing
Ukraine front freezes into a de facto ceasefire line with no settlement; European defence spending rises toward 3% of GDP, funded mostly by borrowing
Fed eases slowly to ~3.25% while US core inflation sticks near 3%; ECB holds at 2%
AI capex boom continues but hyperscaler margins come under scrutiny; first large white-collar layoff waves in back-office and call-centre work
Two hot Northern Hemisphere summers push food prices up; La Nina eases briefly
US election delivers divided government; deficit stays ~6.5% of GDP and a debt-ceiling standoff briefly rattles Treasuries
Japanese 30-year yields breach 4%; BoJ slows QT and buys back long bonds to calm markets
Ethiopia-style restructurings spread: Pakistan and a large West African borrower miss payments, G20 Common Framework stalls again
EU carbon border adjustment fully bites; India and Brazil retaliate with digital-services levies
Gulf tensions flare around Iranian enrichment; oil spikes to $105 for a quarter, pushing G20 inflation to a 3.9% peak
Global growth dips to ~2.1% as AI-equity correction (Nasdaq -28%) hits wealth effects and capex; no outright US recession but unemployment rises to 4.9%
UK and France face a gilt/OAT sell-off after failed budgets; France forms a technocratic caretaker government
China grows ~3.5%, exports deflation via overcapacity in EVs, steel and solar; more countries impose anti-dumping duties
A border war between Ethiopia and Eritrea over sea access draws in Gulf backers - the run's one major new conflict
Central banks cut again; yield curves steepen as term premia rise with debt
Modest recovery: AI agents now standard in software, finance and customer service; productivity gains visible in US data (~0.4pp/yr) but uneven
Global unemployment peaks near 5.6% early in the year as displaced clerical workers struggle to re-match; youth unemployment in North Africa and South Asia drives migration surges
COP35 confirms 2030 pledges missed; emissions roughly flat, coal still rising in South and Southeast Asia
WTO appellate body remains dead; trade increasingly routed through 'connector' economies (Mexico, Vietnam, UAE, Morocco)
A fourth sovereign crisis: an Andean economy loses market access after commodity slump and political crisis
Global public debt crosses 100% of GDP; US interest costs exceed defence spending for third straight year
Populist parties lead polls in several EU states; housing protests and pension-age disputes spark recurring strikes
US-China agree a narrow 'chips and fentanyl' truce, but tariff averages stay near decade highs
Warming trend reaches ~1.56C; a deadly heat dome in South Asia and record wildfire season in the Mediterranean
Firms using AI in production near one third; regulation fragments into US, EU and China regimes

winners: Connector economies such as Mexico, Vietnam, UAE and Morocco that arbitrage bloc rivalry
Owners of AI compute, grid and defence assets
India's services and manufacturing clusters, despite uneven job creation
losers: Frontier-market debtors in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia squeezed by aid cuts and high rates
Mid-skill clerical and back-office workers in rich economies
Young renters in high-cost cities facing housing costs and weak wage growth
bullets: Growth averaged ~2.6% - no collapse, but a 2029 AI-equity correction and bond jitters left output below pre-2026 trend.
Debt kept ratcheting: world public debt ~103% of GDP, US ~133%, Japan managing via BoJ long-bond purchases; term premia are structurally higher.
Four sovereign debt crises, mainly frontier economies, met with slow, piecemeal restructurings rather than a systemic fix.
Trade is more fragmented (index 57): tariffs, export controls and carbon border levies push supply chains through third-country connectors.
AI is mainstream in about a third of firms; ~38 million jobs displaced cumulatively, with gains concentrated in capital and top-skill workers.
Climate action lags: renewables ~41% of electricity, emissions flat rather than falling, warming ~1.56C and costlier extremes.
Politics is sourer: unrest up, trust down, recurring strikes over housing, pensions and cost of living, especially in Europe and emerging cities.
One new major war (Horn of Africa) and frozen conflicts elsewhere keep defence budgets and energy risk premia elevated.
wildcard: A 2029 near-failed Japanese 30-year bond auction that forced the BoJ into emergency long-end purchases and briefly sent the yen to 175 per dollar.
image_description: In a drizzly Lyon suburb in 2031, a former insurance claims clerk now delivering groceries by e-cargo bike waits outside a shuttered bank branch turned AI-help kiosk, while a poster for next week's pension strike peels beside a sign announcing new rent caps.
